1	\section{Conclusion}
2	
3	The dominant vulnerability predictor in LLM judge panels transitions with panel size: $\eta_{\max}$ dominates at $K{=}3$ (bootstrap 5/12, $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ 1/12); at $K{\geq}5$, $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ dominates (7/12, $\eta_{\max}$ 0/12). The aggregate positive $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ association is attack-mechanism-dependent (targeted positive, shared-bias negative); Bayesian calibration reverses it at $K{=}3$ and neutralizes both predictors at $K{=}5$. Observational regression cannot reliably disentangle diversity's causal contribution from the co-occurring capability deficit (\S\ref{sec:analysis}). For deployment: at $K{=}3$, screen for individual robustness and use Bayesian aggregation; at $K{\geq}5$, prefer correlated robustness profiles over maximally independent judges. \paragraph{Diversity--Capability Confound.}
The $r{=}0.70$ correlation between $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and $\eta_{\max}$ ($r{\approx}0.82$ in log space) reflects a structural property: maximizing diversity requires sampling across capability tiers, introducing weaker judges. VIF averages 3.0 (10/12 below 5). After controlling for $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$, $\eta_{\max}$ retains partial $r{=}0.31$ (unique variance ${\approx}9.6\%$); $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$'s partial $r{=}0.12$ (${\approx}1.4\%$). This asymmetry shows the confound does not fully explain $\eta_{\max}$'s advantage, but observational regression cannot reliably disentangle diversity's causal contribution from the co-occurring capability deficit (Appendix~\ref{app:diversity_capability}). Cinelli--Hazlett sensitivity analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity}) reveals heterogeneous robustness: RV ranges from 0.005 to 0.52 across 36 conditions, with the known $\eta_{\max}$ confound exceeding this threshold in 28/36 conditions. Robustness increases with $K$ (RV exceeds $\eta_{\max}$ in 1/12 at $K{=}3$, 3/12 at $K{=}5$, 4/12 at $K{=}7$), paralleling the regime transition; this motivates the capability-matched replication below. The transition does not replicate in the API-only subset ($K{=}5$: $r(K_{\mathrm{eff}}, \eta_{\max}){=}0.85$, VIF${=}4.4$), where collinearity partially inflates $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ standard errors (${\sim}2{\times}$), attenuating its significance from 7/12 (full pool) to 3/12. However, capability-matched subsamples that break this collinearity ($r{=}0.50$) strengthen $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$'s emergence to 9/12, exceeding the full-pool 7/12 (Appendix~\ref{app:robustness_checks}). This pool dependence is itself informative: the transition requires sufficient capability diversity to manifest, rather than being an artifact of including weak judges. Cross-benchmark prediction further supports this interpretation: $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ computed from MMLU MI predicts ARC vulnerability in 14/18 bootstrap conditions, with cross-benchmark $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ correlations of $r{\approx}0.76$--$0.78$ (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_benchmark}).

\paragraph{Diversity--Capability Confound.}
The $r{=}0.70$ correlation between $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and $\eta_{\max}$ reflects a structural property: maximizing diversity requires sampling across capability tiers, introducing weaker judges. VIF averages 3.0 (10/12 below 5), but observational regression cannot reliably disentangle diversity's causal contribution from the co-occurring capability deficit (Appendix~\ref{app:diversity_capability}). In the full pool, $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$'s independent effect cannot be separated from capability variance in the majority of conditions: Cinelli--Hazlett sensitivity analysis \citep{cinelli2020making} shows that the known $\eta_{\max}$ confound exceeds the robustness value in 28/36 conditions (Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity}). Robustness increases with $K$ (RV exceeds $\eta_{\max}$ in 1/12 at $K{=}3$, 3/12 at $K{=}5$, 4/12 at $K{=}7$), paralleling the regime transition. The API-only subset ($r{=}0.85$) does not replicate the transition (3/12), raising the possibility that $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ partly proxies for quantization-induced capability variance rather than a pure diversity signal. Capability-matched subsampling ($r{=}0.50$, 9 models, 126 panels at $K{=}5$) provides partial mitigation: $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ strengthens to 9/12 and Cinelli--Hazlett RV exceeds the $\eta_{\max}$ confound in 6/12 conditions (conservatively 5/12 excluding near-zero $R^2$; Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity_poolA}), compared to 3/12 in the full pool. Cross-benchmark prediction further supports this: MMLU-derived $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ predicts ARC vulnerability in 14/18 conditions ($r{\approx}0.76$--$0.78$; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_benchmark}). The transition is thus a descriptive regime shift whose independent causal attribution to diversity requires capability-controlled experimental designs.
